# FERB.app (notch UI, intro, sounds) (area `app`)

The Mac app the owner uses: notch, chat, settings, setup intro, orb, sounds, preview window, playground. The owner's side; talks to the daemon only through its RPC.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **APP-1** (owner): FERB.app's setup offers "Give FERB its own Google account (recommended)": the owner creates the account (creation needs human verification) and signs it into a browser profile; FERB finds and pairs it. If skipped, FERB browses as the owner in a profile the owner picks, and features that need FERB's own inbox say they aren't set up.
- **APP-2** (owner): FERB.app has, functional only (the owner polishes the UI later): Restore, listing FERB's Trash moves, backup copies and snapshots and restoring one; Delete, removing a stored owner secret or card; Uninstall, removing FERB fully, Keychain items included. Daemon RPCs plus minimal app screens.
- **APP-3** (owner): A button on each message in the notch opens the screenshot taken when it was sent and the images its task captured, each exactly as the model got it, with time and app or site. Settings → Data lists every saved screenshot of the last 7 days, newest first.
- **APP-4** (agent): FERB.app's how-tos, shortcuts and setting places are one list kept in NotchCore (AppGuide), beside the screens it names. FERB.app sends it with about.guide (APP_ONLY: only FERB.app's words become FERB's guide) on every connection; the daemon keeps it in memory and, until the app connects after a daemon start, the About document says so.
- **APP-5** (agent): FERB.app's Uninstall (plain or delete everything) awaits SMAppService.unregister() and checks the status; only not-registered or not-found goes on to `ferb uninstall [--purge --yes]`. A throw or a service macOS still lists shows why in the output lines and nothing is uninstalled.
- **APP-300** (owner): The notch shows the turn card with one row per part and its states (working spinner, done check, asks amber, couldn't-do red, updated tag, paused violet), the done/sites footer, questions with buttons inside a row, the plan-line bubble style and the typing-dots bubble; not the mock's dashed explanation labels or "code" chips. The UI work is functional; the owner polishes.
- **APP-301** (owner): When a part needs the owner (a question or a Yes) and when the whole task finishes, the notch opens itself without taking keyboard focus or switching apps. Rows that fill quietly only update the card. A macOS banner is the fallback only when the notch can't show (a full-screen app or video covers it, the display is asleep, FERB.app is quit); tapping it opens the notch.
- **APP-400** (agent): Before it starts the app, FERB.app's executable answers `transcribe`, `status` and `request-speech` with the old helper's arguments, answer files, lease and exit codes (no window, no microphone). The daemon runs it with `open -g -n -W --env FERB_HOME=… <FERB.app> --args <mode> …`. `request-speech` stays but setup no longer calls it. The home rule is NotchCore/FerbHomeRule.swift.
- **APP-401** (agent): Setup has no separate hearing row: the microphone row covers Microphone and Speech Recognition (one grant for dictation and hearing); `ferb doctor` still probes hearing.
- **APP-402** (agent): Settings → General "Send dictation when I let go of the keys" (`voice.sendOnRelease`) is off by default. A sent draft that still holds the last dictated words goes with `speak: true`, so a dictated message lightly edited and sent with Return is still answered aloud; a typed message isn't.
- **APP-403** (owner): The notch shows a live picture of what FERB is working on: the task's own browser tab or the one Mac app window the current call targets, never the whole screen. The work-row circles, the popover and the floating player stream while a task runs.
- **APP-404** (owner): When FERB stops working in a window (moves to another step, pauses, waits, asks), the preview freezes on FERB's last frame of it and shows what FERB is doing now over it (asking, waiting, working in another app, paused). It never keeps streaming the owner's window after FERB has left it.
- **APP-405** (owner): There is no preview frame-rate cap until the heat is confirmed from data. Preview frames and capture time are counted (`resource_samples.work_json.preview`); step 13 measures the same task with the preview open vs closed, and the owner decides a cap from that.
- **APP-406** (owner): The preview popovers and the floating player are excluded from screen sharing and screen recordings (`sharingType = .none`).
- **APP-407** (agent): Every preview loop pauses while the displays sleep, the screen is locked or another user's session is in front (`PreviewAccess`); each video view asks only while its window is visible (occlusion); the work-row circles only while the notch is open and not stepped aside. The frame rate itself is unchanged (APP-405).
